title: PP Engine Wiring — LineByLine, SLD Rewriter, Probing, Thread Milling
description: Wire the 4 highest-impact orphaned engines into the PP pipeline. LineByLineAdaptiveEngine replaces 8 simplified inline Phase 2 stages with 10 physics-complete modules. StabilityRPMRewriterEngine adds SLD-aware G-code RPM rewriting (unique in industry). ProbingCycleEngine replaces the Stage 6.2 stub with multi-dialect probing. ThreadMillingPhysicsEngine adds thread class prediction from deflection physics.

engines: ThreadMillingPhysicsEngine (1,228 lines) — helical kinematics + thread class prediction
TappingTorqueEngine (337 lines) — tapping torque + breakage risk
ChatterStabilityLobeEngine — SLD data source for RPM rewriter
formulas: Chip thinning factor CTF = 1/sqrt(1-(1-ae/D)^2) — in LineByLineAdaptiveEngine
Kienzle radial/axial thread forces — in ThreadMillingPhysicsEngine
tribal: controller-knowledge.json — probing macro numbers per controller

forge_triple.protective_hook: pp-engine-wiring-check — blocks PP edits that duplicate existing engine logic inline instead of calling the engine
forge_triple.mcp_action: prism_cam post_process_enhanced — post-process with all enhanced engines active
forge_triple.skill: /pp-enhanced — run post-processor with LineByLine + SLD rewrite + probing + threading

units.title: Add LineByLineAdaptiveEngine to _getEngine() and wire as Stage 2.0
steps: Read LineByLineAdaptiveEngine.ts fully — understand its 10 modules (chip thinning, engagement-adaptive feed, corner decel, arc/plunge limits, wear+thermal tracking, entry/exit optimizer, S-curve feed smoothing, chip evacuation, block density)
Add to _getEngine() lazy loader as 'lineByLine'
Add StageConfig flag: line_by_line_adaptive (default: true)
Wire as Stage 2.0: after Phase 1 physics but before existing Phase 2 inline stages
Pass current G-code string + tool/material/machine params to lineByLineAdaptiveEngine.optimize()
Map OptimizedLine[] result back to ToolpathBlock[] — update feed, speed, add per-line annotations
When line_by_line_adaptive=true, SKIP existing inline Phase 2 stages 2.1-2.7 (they duplicate this engine)
When false, fall back to existing inline stages for backward compat
exit_conditions: New test: LineByLine produces per-line feed annotations with physics reasons
New test: cycle time delta reported in analytics
New test: disable flag falls back to inline Phase 2 without regression

units.title: Wire StabilityRPMRewriterEngine as Stage 3.5 — SLD-aware G-code RPM rewriting
steps: Read StabilityRPMRewriterEngine.ts — understand rewrite() method
Add to _getEngine() as 'stabilityRewriter'
Add StageConfig flag: stability_rewrite (default: true)
Wire as Stage 3.5: after motion dynamics (3.2) and smoothing (3.1), before Phase 4
Pass current G-code string + SLD data from Stage 1.3 (StochasticChatterEngine result)
Call stabilityRPMRewriter.rewrite(gcodeStr, { lobes, toolFlutes, currentDoc, feedPerTooth, minRPM: machine.min_rpm, maxRPM: machine.max_rpm })
Report RPM changes in analytics: sld_rpm_rewrites count, avg_shift, chatter_risk assessment
exit_conditions: New test: G-code with S3000 near chatter zone gets rewritten to stable pocket
New test: feed adjusted proportionally to maintain chip load after RPM shift

units.title: Replace Stage 6.2 hardcoded G65 stub with ProbingCycleEngine
steps: Read ProbingCycleEngine.ts — understand generate() method, 4 controller dialects, 12 probe operations
Add to _getEngine() as 'probingCycle'
In Stage 6.2 (probe_routines), replace the hardcoded G65 P9810 loop with:
Map machine.controller to ProbeController: fanuc/haas → renishaw_fanuc/renishaw_haas, heidenhain → heidenhain, siemens → siemens
Infer probe operations from program context: first XY → corner probe, Z surface → surface_z, circular pocket → bore, boss → boss
Call probingCycleEngine.generate({ controller, operations, wcs, toolNumber }) for each inferred operation
Append generated probing G-code to output (separate section or prepended setup block)
Add probe_routines_generated to analytics
exit_conditions: New test: Fanuc controller generates Renishaw G65 P981x probing
New test: Siemens controller generates CYCLE977/978 probing
New test: Heidenhain controller generates TCH PROBE cycles
Analytics report shows probe_routines_generated count and types

units.title: Wire ThreadMillingPhysicsEngine for thread operations — thread class prediction
steps: Read ThreadMillingPhysicsEngine.ts — helical kinematics, force modeling, deflection→pitch error→thread class
Add to _getEngine() as 'threadMilling'
Add StageConfig flag: thread_milling_physics (default: true)
Detect thread milling operations: tool type = thread_mill + helical G2/G3 blocks, or tap_cycle blocks
Wire as Stage 1.8 (after deflection 1.5, before chip morphology 1.6):
Call threadMillingPhysicsEngine.helicalKinematics() for Vc correction
Call threadMillingPhysicsEngine.cuttingForces() for radial/axial force components
Call threadMillingPhysicsEngine.deflectionError() for pitch diameter error
Call threadMillingPhysicsEngine.threadQuality() for thread class prediction (6H/6g etc.)
Attach thread_quality to ToolpathBlock: { predicted_class, deflection_mm, within_tolerance, recommendations }
Feed warnings to Phase 5 safety output if thread class degrades below spec
exit_conditions: New test: M12x1.75 thread milling predicts thread class from deflection
New test: excessive feed degrades predicted class with warning
New test: non-thread operations skip this stage cleanly
Thread quality appears in analytics report

exit_gate: All 4 engines wired. LineByLine as Stage 2.0, SLD Rewriter as Stage 3.4b, Probing as Stage 6.2, ThreadMilling as Stage 1.5b. 219/219 tests pass across 6 files.
